text: The Patriots delivered an emphatic statement in their Week 2 home opener against Pittsburgh, as the defense absolutely suffocated Aaron Rodgers in a dominant 20-3 victory highlighted by TreVeyon Henderson's season-debut performance—the running back punching in a 39-yard touchdown run while Eli Ponder added a 19-yard fumble recovery for a score to pad New England's lead. Henderson and wide receiver Efton Chism III both made their season debuts after sitting out Week 1, providing the offense with fresh weapons against the vaunted Steelers defense that had been a major preseason talking point around quarterback Drake Maye's development. The victory came with a cost, however, as starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off with an ankle injury late in the first quarter, potentially creating immediate depth concerns along the offensive line. In an emotional footnote to the weekend, Stephon Gilmore—the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro—signed a one-day contract to retire as a member of the Patriots, closing the book on one of the most decorated defensive careers in franchise history.
